parsed.summary: Because you reported a right-shoulder problem during swims (most recently with injury reported on 2026-08-06) the plan begins with a short, shoulder-protected week to avoid loading the painful catch/overhead pattern while you recover. You said you don’t want total rest and that cycling and running are fine, so we maintain triathlon shape with extra bike/run volume and swim work that avoids painful loading, then progressively reintroduce full swim load and open-water practice so you can hit the 1500 m and ride-volume targets before the Hamburg Olympic-distance on 2027-07-11. If the shoulder remains persistent or worsens at any point, take that to a healthcare professional for assessment.

phases.title: Shoulder-protected (maintain triathlete feel)
phases.focus: Protect the right shoulder by avoiding overhead/catch loading for one week while keeping you feeling like a triathlete: increased bike and run volume, mobility and daily thoracic/shoulder prehab, and swim sessions that use minimal shoulder load (kick, fins, snorkel, or non‑catch drills).

phases.title: Base endurance — accumulate bike/run volume
phases.focus: Build aerobic base and weekly bike volume safely while continuing daily mobility work and controlled, low-load swim maintenance so you don’t lose swim feel. This phase prioritises steady progression on the bike and run to prepare for later specific ride volume weeks.

phases.title: Strength, mobility and gradual swim reintroduction
phases.focus: Introduce progressive dryland shoulder and core strength, maintain thoracic mobility, and slowly reintroduce progressive swim technique work — avoid full catch loading until pain-free — while keeping a steady bike/run base. The aim is to restore a pain-tolerant freestyle stroke and build the strength foundation needed for longer swims.

phases.title: Specific volume for the ride target
phases.focus: Shift to higher weekly bike volume and structured long rides with one planned week targeting the 200 km ride-week goal (progressive overload, recovery weeks built in). Continue controlled swim progression and keep runs as maintenance/quality sessions.

phases.title: Open-water swim consolidation and sustained endurance
phases.focus: Focus on open-water skill development and progressive long swims to reach a continuous 1500 m by 2027-05-30, while sustaining bike and run endurance. Continue shoulder prehab and only restore full catch load when pain-free during controlled progressions.

phases.title: Race-specific sharpening for Hamburg Olympic-distance
phases.focus: Final preparation: simulate race pacing and transitions, reduce overall volume while keeping key intensity sessions for swim, bike and run, and prioritise recovery and shoulder maintenance so you arrive ready on 2027-07-11.

sessions.title: Easy turbo endurance
sessions.intent: Maintain aerobic base with an easy, conversational turbo ride that does not load your shoulder. We're avoiding freestyle catch work this week because you reported shoulder problems on 2026-08-02 and 2026-08-06; if it persists or worsens, get it checked by a healthcare professional.

sessions.title: Easy run with strides
sessions.intent: Keep running fitness with an easy 30–35 minute run plus 6×20s strides; should feel relaxed with short, controlled pickups. No shoulder involvement — focus on cadence and leg turnover.

sessions.title: Strength — lower body & core (no shoulder loading)
sessions.intent: Build leg and core strength with single-leg work, glute-ham moves and anti-rotation core; avoid any overhead or heavy horizontal pulling/pressing that loads the right shoulder. Controlled, moderately hard sets that preserve shoulder rest.

sessions.title: Turbo threshold intervals
sessions.intent: Raise cycling threshold with 3×10–12 minute efforts at steady hard effort, easy spin between; bike-only work so your shoulder remains unloaded. Should be challenging but sustainable and well-managed.

sessions.title: Pool — aqua jogging + mobility
sessions.intent: Keep water familiarity without stressing the catch: 25–30 minutes of aqua jogging/water running plus 10 minutes of gentle thoracic and shoulder mobility that does not load the shoulder. This preserves swim-specific comfort while protecting the injured area.

sessions.title: Long steady road ride
sessions.intent: Accumulate time-in-saddle with an easy-to-steady 2-hour ride to build endurance without any overhead shoulder work. Keep effort mostly easy; use this to increase weekly bike volume safely.
